title: SQL  POWER() Function - GeeksforGeeks
content:
The POWER() function in SQL is a mathematical function used to raise a number to the power of another number. It returns the result of the specified base number raised to the specified exponent.

  • Useful for mathematical and numerical calculations.
  • Used with integer and decimal values.

Syntax

POWER(number, exponent)
  • number: The base number that you want to raise to a power.
  • exponent: The power to which the number is raised.

Note: The POWER() function is supported by MySQL, SQL Server, PostgreSQL and Oracle. SQLite does not provide POWER() as a standard built-in function.

Examples

Below are some examples of the POWER() function to understand how it is used in different situations.

Example 1: Calculate the Square of a Number

In this example, we will calculate the square of 5.

Query:

SELECT POWER(5, 2) AS square;

Output:

Example 2: Calculate the Cube of a Number

In this example, we will calculate the cube of 4.

Query:

SELECT POWER(4, 3) AS cube;

Output:

Example 3: Use POWER() on a Table Column

Let us create a products table containing product prices.

Now, we can use the POWER() function to calculate the square of each product price.

Query:

SELECT product_name,
       price,
       POWER(price, 2) AS price_square
FROM products;

Output:

  • Calculates the square of each value in the price column.
  • Returns the calculated values as price_square.
